deviation: No flow through SDV-101 on a spurious HIPPS trip
causes: 1oo2 pressure transmitter drift or failure: a single PT reaching the trip threshold closes SDV-101, since 1oo2 has no 2oo3 voting
Plugged PT impulse tapping (hydrate, wax or iron-carbonate corrosion product) giving a false high signal
HIPPS logic-solver card or power-supply fault; partial-stroke test left in the tripped state
Common-cause impulse-line or root-valve isolation error during routine calibration
consequences: Instant loss of 137.1 MMscfd sales gas and 2,936 bbl/d condensate; all three compression trains lose HP feed
Wells continue to flow against a closed SDV-101 at up to 95 bara; flowline/wellhead cooldown and possible hydrate or wax deposition before restart
Restart needs full HIPPS reset and HP inlet repressurisation; the four-week shutdown plan assumes no unplanned trip
severity_reason: A production and restart event on the whole export stream with no direct loss of containment, but repeated spurious trips push operators toward HIPPS bypass.

deviation: SDV-101 does not close on a HIPPS demand (failure to close)
causes: Sand/condensate erosion of the 316L/Duplex trim or seat, so the valve passes the wellstream after the trip
Actuator spring or solenoid failure, or loss of instrument air, leaving the valve open
Proof testing limited to a partial-stroke test (about 80-90% travel); full-stroke closure is not proven between 12-month proof tests
Single final element: 1oo2 transmitters and HFT 1 do not give a redundant valve
consequences: V-101 and the 66 barg inlet pipeline are exposed to 95 bara wellhead pressure; the 72.6 bara maximum incidental pressure is exceeded
PSV-101 alone must pass the full 42.63 kg/s blocked-outlet case (91.1% of the flare now, 107.5% after the +18% re-rate)
Loss of containment at the HP separator or inlet spool with hydrocarbon jet-fire/explosion potential
severity_reason: Failure of the only pressure barrier between a 95 bara wellstream and a 66 barg vessel and pipeline is major-accident potential.

deviation: HP inlet pressure above the 66 barg design (wellhead up to 95 bara)
causes: Well control or choke failure, or a surging well delivering close to the 95 bara shut-in pressure
The HIPPS trip setpoint is not stated in the basis, so the margin between trip and the 66 barg PSV set is undefined
PT calibration error or a blocked tapping reading low, delaying the trip
consequences: The inlet line and pipeline see up to 72.6 bara maximum incidental pressure, the NORSOK S-001 two-barrier case
If the trip is late the PSV lifts at 66 barg and the flare is at 91.1% now and 107.5% at the re-rated rate
V-101 shell and nozzles at 110% of design pressure with only 3 mm corrosion allowance on a ten-year-old SA-516-70N shell
severity_reason: An undefined trip margin on the primary overpressure barrier can put a 66 barg vessel and pipeline above design pressure.

deviation: Wellstream above 363 K (90 C) at SDV-101 and V-101
causes: Hot well or reduced Joule-Thomson cooling as the choke is opened for rate
Inhibitor or chemical injection at higher temperature, or a workover returning hotter fluid
consequences: Only 10 K margin to the 100 C design temperature of SDV-101 and V-101
316L HIPPS seals, gaskets and wetted parts approach their limit, and the CO2 inhibition basis (0.15 mm/yr at 81 C) is no longer qualified
severity_reason: A slow overtemperature that damages nothing immediately but invalidates the materials and corrosion basis.

deviation: Only one of the two HIPPS pressure transmitters is in service
causes: 1oo2 transmitters on a common impulse tapping or root valve, so a single plugging event disables both
One PT isolated for calibration without a bypass permit or a compensating trip
Diagnostic coverage of 0.6 leaves 40% of dangerous undetected failures
consequences: Protection degrades from SIL 3 (PFD 1e-4) to a single transmitter (order 1e-3), so the 35% relief credit cannot be claimed
PSV-101 becomes the only barrier, and its flare margin is already consumed
severity_reason: A degraded but detectable protection state that only becomes a hazard if a pressure excursion coincides.

deviation: HIPPS bypassed or proof-tested with the HP inlet live
causes: The 12-month proof test and partial-stroke test are performed on a live train under a bypass permit
Bypass left in place after the test or after a nuisance trip
No independent high-pressure trip; the PSV is the only protection while bypassed
consequences: Zero SIL-3 protection above the 66 barg PSV set; a well surge then relies on a PSV and a flare already at 91.1%
A bypass left active converts every later overpressure into a PSV-only event without the 35% credit
severity_reason: A defeated SIL-3 function on the primary overpressure barrier is a recognised major-accident precursor.

deviation: HP interface level high: water into the oil outlet
causes: LCV-102 stuck or plugged by scale or sand in the 8 in water draw-off
Interface level transmitter fouled by emulsion or wax
Water rate rising with the cut toward 57% while the weir and interface control are unchanged
The internals change (K 0.11 to 0.14) alters the flow field without re-tuning the interface control
consequences: Water is carried under with the oil into the two-phase V-102 and V-103, which have no water draw-off
Condensate export off-spec (BS&W) and water accumulation in the stock tank
At the extreme, water covers the gas outlet and carries over to K-101
severity_reason: Water misrouting degrades product and can reach the compressors, but needs a second failure to become a release.

deviation: HP interface level low: water carried under with the oil
causes: LCV-102 fails open or is driven open by a faulty level signal
Oil-leg level control (LIC-101) draining the interface
Water draw-off above the incoming 2,782 bbl/d during a rate change
consequences: Water enters V-102 at 10 bara, flashes and accumulates with no boot, then is carried to K-102A or the stock tank
Water carryover to the compression suction, which has no knock-out drum, risks impeller erosion and seal damage
severity_reason: Water to the compressor is a credible damage path; the low level is recoverable if the interface is detected.

deviation: HP gas rate above separator capacity (99.8% at K 0.11; 118.9% at 163.4 MMscfd)
causes: Choke opened toward the 163.4 MMscfd well potential before the internals are changed
Vendor K 0.14 not achieved, leaving the cap near 137.4 MMscfd
Higher gas/oil ratio than the year-ten forecast as the C7+ fraction falls
consequences: Vane-pack flooding and liquid carryover to K-101; only 0.3 MMscfd of margin at the base case
After the internals change the cap is 174.9 MMscfd, so the 163.4 MMscfd potential sits at 93.4% with little margin
severity_reason: Operation above the Souders-Brown limit causes carryover and compressor damage but is bounded by the 174.9 MMscfd cap.

deviation: Liquid (oil/water) carryover in the HP gas to K-101
causes: Gas rate at or above the K factor; mist-eliminator damage or fouling
Foaming or emulsion at a 48.7% water cut and rising
High oil level covering the gas outlet during a level upset
consequences: There is no K-101 suction knock-out drum or coalescer: liquid reaches the impellers and dry-gas seals
Erosion, rotor imbalance and seal failure with a potential gas fire; sales gas contaminated
1,869 mol/s of HP gas is the whole export stream, so any trip loses the full rate
severity_reason: Liquid carryover into a centrifugal compressor with no suction scrubber is a credible seal-failure and fire path.

deviation: Water cut above 48.7% drives retention below the 6.5 min minimum
causes: Field water breakthrough to the 57% end-of-forecast cut
Emulsion or foam reducing the effective settling volume
Total liquid flow rising while the weir and interface setting stay fixed
consequences: Water retention of 7.83 min at 48.7% falls to about 6.7 min at 57%, cutting the margin from 1.3 min to about 0.2 min
Interface settling is already 17.09 s against a 60 s class check, so the coalescer carries the whole duty
Water carryover to the oil and condensate, and overboard oil in the produced water
severity_reason: The separator is at its performance limit by design; the coalescer is the only barrier between this and routine carryover.

deviation: Loss of LIC-102 or instrument air, with LCV-102 failing open and gas blowing by to the 25 barg water package
causes: Instrument-air loss with a fail-open or undefined fail position on LCV-102
LCV-102 seat or trim erosion after ten years, passing gas at a normal liquid level
Level transmitter failure driving the valve fully open
consequences: 60 bara gas into V-104 and V-105 (25 barg design) and the 8 in ANSI 300 water line
Overpressure and rupture of the coalescer or hydrocyclone, with hydrocarbon release to the water deck
No PSV is shown on V-104 or V-105 in the basis
severity_reason: A 60 bara source connected to a 25 barg package with no relief is a vessel-rupture scenario.

deviation: V-102 overpressure above its 10 bara duty
causes: VLV-102 fails open, passing 60 bara HP liquid and gas into V-102
K-102A trip or MP gas outlet blockage with the letdown still open
V-102 level control failure, or carryover blocking the gas outlet
consequences: V-102 (existing, 3 mm corrosion allowance) above its 10 bara design; its relief case is not in the basis, which specifies only PSV-101
Gas blowby to V-103 and the stock tank, or loss of containment at the MP vessel
severity_reason: The MP vessel is probably protected by its own PSV, but that relief path is absent from the frozen basis, so the case is unverified.

deviation: V-102 liquid level high with carryover to K-102A
causes: VLV-102 overfeeding after a level or flow upset
LP letdown (VLV-103) restricted or V-103 backed up
Water accumulation from HP carry-under raising the apparent level
consequences: Liquid into K-102A, which has no suction scrubber: erosion, imbalance and seal damage on one of the three MP trains
MP gas rate to the sales mixer falls and the export compressor sees a changed flow split
severity_reason: Local compressor damage and a train trip, recoverable if the level is caught before a slug.

deviation: Water carried into the two-phase MP and LP stages, which have no water draw-off
causes: HP interface low or an emulsion passing water with the oil
V-102 and V-103 are two-phase by design, with no boot or water draw-off
An upset in the HP water draw-off (node 2) sending water with the oil
consequences: Water accumulates in V-102 and V-103 and is eventually carried to K-102A, K-103A or the stock tank
Condensate off-spec and water in the 6 in export line; up to 2,782 bbl/d can be misrouted
Corrosion of the carbon-steel MP and LP vessels and lines, where the 3 mm allowance and CO2 inhibition assume the water leaves at V-101
severity_reason: The two-phase MP and LP design has no water sink, so any HP water slip propagates to the product and the compressors.

deviation: Cold start after the four-week shutdown with hydrate or ice in VLV-102 and V-102
causes: Wet gas (13.45 mol% water) at 10 bara entering a vessel at ambient -5 C
No hydrate inhibitor, and flow assurance is explicitly excluded from the basis
Restart before V-102 is warmed through
consequences: Hydrate or ice plug in the letdown or MP gas line, with overpressure upstream at VLV-102
Delayed first gas and a second depressurisation of the MP stage
severity_reason: A startup transient that can plug the MP stage and delay first gas; recoverable but schedule-critical.

deviation: Stock-tank flash gas routed to the 90 bara sales header without a compressor
causes: V-104 at 1.013 bara is connected to the sales-gas mixer at 90 bara in the PFD, while the VRU and fourth stage are deferred
No flash-gas compressor in the scope, so the route is non-physical
Flash line blocked or undersized
consequences: The stock tank cannot vent to the sales header; it is back-pressured and the flash gas is vented or flared instead
Lost condensate and vapour recovery, plus a VOC emission source; the mass balance that gives 161.8 MMscfd depends on this stream
severity_reason: A design-basis inconsistency that changes the product slate and creates a vent and overpressure path, but not an immediate release.

deviation: V-104 stock tank overfill or LP liquid carryover
causes: P-101 trip or condensate line backpressure stopping export
V-103 level high with liquid carryover through E-104
E-104 flooding or a blocked condensate flash line
consequences: 2,936 bbl/d of condensate overflows to the deck or drain, creating fire and pollution risk
Liquid carryover to the flash-gas route and the sales header
severity_reason: A large flammable liquid release on an offshore deck; ignition depends on the drain and hot-work state.

deviation: E-104 outlet below 288 K with wax or ice in V-104 and the 6 in condensate line
causes: Cooler over-performance at -5 C ambient or a colder letdown at VLV-103
Wet condensate (water carried under) freezing in the stock tank
A wax cloud point above 288 K for the gassier year-ten condensate
consequences: Wax or ice plugging the 15 km, 25 bara condensate line and losing condensate export
Overpressure upstream of the plug between P-101 and the blockage
severity_reason: A blocked export line with a pump upstream can overpressure the 6 in line; blockage is recoverable but costly.

deviation: Free water in the stock tank and the condensate export
causes: Water carry-under from V-101 through the two-phase MP and LP stages
No water draw-off on V-104, and E-104 condenses water at 288 K
An emulsion not broken by the HP internals change
consequences: Condensate off-spec (BS&W) at the 2,936-3,466 bbl/d export rate
Wet CO2 corrosion of the 6 in X65 line with 3 mm allowance, and reception penalties
severity_reason: A product-quality and integrity issue on the condensate export line with no immediate safety consequence.

deviation: Compressor surge at low flow, including after the re-rate
causes: Turndown to 60% of design, with new impellers moving the surge line and the antisurge recycle not re-tuned
K-101 trip while K-102 and K-103 continue to discharge into the 90 bara mixer
A blocked or restricted export line (node 8) raising discharge pressure
consequences: Surge cycles damage thrust bearings and dry-gas seals, and a seal failure releases HP gas
Trip of the export train, loss of 137.1-161.8 MMscfd, and a V-101 overpressure and flare event
severity_reason: Surge is a credible machinery-damage and seal-leak path, and the re-rate changes the curve without a documented antisurge re-verification.

deviation: K-101 power above the driver (2,689 kW against 2,300 kW, 116.9%)
causes: Well potential of 163.4 MMscfd reached before the driver re-rate is complete
Fouled intercoolers or aftercooler, or 35 C ambient, raising absorbed power
A higher gas molecular weight or a changed flow split from the MP and LP trains
Stage count is inconsistent: the basis says one stage, the datasheet and P&ID show two, so the re-rate curve is ambiguous
consequences: Driver overload trip or motor damage, losing the export train and triggering a V-101 overpressure event
The re-rate is the 22-week long-lead item, so the facility can be at 163.4 MMscfd on the old driver
severity_reason: An overload trip is recoverable, but the sequence (trip to flare) is the same as a blocked outlet.

deviation: K-101 suction below 60 bara
causes: V-101 pressure low on turndown or after a HIPPS or SDV closure
K-101 surge or a restricted gas outlet
HP separator liquid level high, reducing the gas space
consequences: Compression ratio rises, discharge temperature and power rise, and the driver trips
V-101 liquid flashes, feeding two-phase flow to the compressor
severity_reason: High-ratio operation is outside the re-rate envelope and couples directly to liquid carryover.

deviation: Reverse flow from the 90 bara sales mixer into a tripped K-102 or K-103 train
causes: Discharge check-valve failure on a train that has tripped
Startup with the sales header already at 90 bara
K-102C or K-103E trip while the other trains hold the header
consequences: 90 bara gas into intercoolers and compressor casings designed for 4-43 bara stage pressure
Rupture of a low-pressure intercooler or casing with gas release and fire
severity_reason: Reverse flow into equipment rated far below 90 bara is a vessel-rupture scenario.

deviation: Liquid or water into K-101, K-102A or K-103A
causes: Separator carryover (nodes 2 and 3); no suction knock-out drums on any train
Higher mist carryover at the K 0.14 gas velocity
Water from the two-phase MP and LP stages
consequences: Impeller erosion, imbalance, dry-gas-seal damage and a potential gas fire
Intercooler fouling and reduced capacity, forcing an unplanned train outage
severity_reason: Liquid ingestion is a credible seal and impeller damage path; escalation to fire needs a seal failure.

deviation: Loss of power, instrument air or cooling to the three trains
causes: Platform power failure or air-compressor trip
Cooling-medium loss, or 35 C ambient defeating the 313.15 K aftercooler approach
A common cause acting on the utilities shared by all three trains
consequences: All trains trip; V-101 overpressure and 42.63 kg/s to the flare, at 91.1% now and 107.5% after the re-rate
Loss of export and a black start, with the flare as the only pressure sink
severity_reason: A total compression trip converts directly into the governing relief case on a flare that has no margin after the re-rate.

deviation: No flow through the produced-water package (P-102 trip or blockage)
causes: Single P-102 with no installed spare; a power or seal failure stops the only pump
Hydrocyclone liner or coalescer plugging by solids or scale, or reject-valve failure
The datasheet duty (18.4 m3/h) is the current 2,782 bbl/d, not the 39.7 m3/h needed for 6,000 bbl/d
consequences: Water backs up to V-101: only 7.83 min of water retention at 2,782 bbl/d (about 8 min) before the interface reaches the oil and gas outlet
Oil to the gas outlet and compressor, or water to the condensate; the facility must cut rate or trip
severity_reason: The water plant is the hidden capacity link (92.7% now); its loss reaches the HP separator within minutes.

deviation: Water rate above package capacity, or one 50% hydrocyclone liner blocked
causes: Water cut rising to 57% (about 3,250 bbl/d) with one of the two 50% liners out
Reject control valve failure or a surge from V-101
The old 3,000 bbl/d plant is already at 92.7% before the upgrade
consequences: Hydrocyclone and coalescer overload, oil-in-water above permit, and water backup to V-101
Before the upgrade the water plant caps gas at 147.8 MMscfd, stranding the compressor and flare capacity
severity_reason: A capacity and quality exceedance with an environmental permit consequence, but no direct loss of containment.

deviation: Produced water at 81 C against an 80 C package design
causes: V-101 operates at 354.15 K (81 C) and there is no produced-water cooler
A hot well or reduced Joule-Thomson cooling raising the HP separator temperature
consequences: No design-temperature margin on V-104, V-105 and P-102
316L is at risk of chloride pitting or stress-corrosion cracking at 80 C in chloride-bearing produced water, and elastomer and gasket limits are reached
severity_reason: A materials-integrity finding with a credible leak path on a 25 barg package, but slow-acting.

deviation: Oil carryover to overboard or reinjection water
causes: Interface settling is 17.09 s against a 60 s class check, so the coalescer is the only barrier
Coalescer bypass or media damage, or an emulsion from the HP separator
Solids loading the coalescer
consequences: Oil-in-water permit exceedance on 2,782 bbl/d of produced water
Reinjection-well fouling and loss of disposal capacity
severity_reason: An environmental permit breach and a disposal-capacity risk; the coalescer is mandatory for exactly this reason.

deviation: Reverse flow from the disposal or reinjection header into the 25 barg package
causes: Disposal well shut-in or reinjection header pressure above 25 barg
P-102 discharge check-valve failure
No PSV on V-104 or V-105; the 8 in 316L line is ANSI 300
consequences: V-105 (25 barg design) overpressured from downstream, with coalescer rupture and produced-water and hydrocarbon release
In the extreme, backflow into V-101 through a failed LCV-102
severity_reason: A 25 barg package with no relief and a higher-pressure downstream source is a rupture scenario.

deviation: Loss of flare: flare or header out of service while HP is live
causes: Flare tip and header replacement, the 25% fallback scope being a four-week tip and header job
Flare isolated with a blind or valve for maintenance while wells are online
Pilot fuel or purge loss, or header liquid blockage extinguishing the flare
consequences: PSV-101 has no disposal route, so V-101 exceeds 66 barg on a blocked outlet
The HIPPS becomes the only barrier, and its 35% credit assumes the flare exists
severity_reason: Loss of the final relief path with a 60 bara gas inventory behind it is a classic major-accident scenario.

deviation: PSV-101 inlet blocked (block valve closed, corrosion products, hydrate)
causes: Inlet isolation valve left closed or car-sealed after PSV re-certification
Iron-carbonate or CO2 corrosion products, or hydrate and ice, in the 4 in inlet
PSV installed with a blind or a restricted inlet spool
consequences: PSV fails to lift; V-101 goes above 66 barg toward and beyond the 72.6 bara maximum incidental pressure
Loss of containment; the HIPPS is then the only barrier and is not a relief device
severity_reason: An isolated or plugged PSV removes the second pressure barrier on a 66 barg vessel.

deviation: PSV outlet or header back pressure derates the conventional PSV
causes: The 6 in PSV outlet must carry 42.63 kg/s at 1.5 barg, of order 40 m3/s, far above a 6 in tailpipe
Flare header at 91.1% now and 107.5% after the re-rate, with liquid in the header
A restricted or blocked tailpipe, or superimposed back pressure above the 1.5 bar design assumption
consequences: A conventional PSV loses capacity as back pressure rises: chattering, reduced lift, and V-101 overpressure
The 6.38 in2 orifice passes the mass, but the outlet rather than the orifice becomes the constraint
severity_reason: The relief path downstream of the orifice is not demonstrated for the governing case, so the PSV may not relieve.

deviation: PSV set pressure equals the vessel design (66 barg), with maximum incidental pressure at 72.6 bara
causes: PSV set at design pressure by basis, with no margin for set-point drift
The blocked-outlet case takes V-101 to 72.6 bara, 110% of design
Back pressure or a slow-opening PSV adding to the accumulated pressure
consequences: Any set-point error or back pressure puts the 66 barg shell above design; relief at 110% is the maximum the code allows and leaves no margin on a ten-year-old shell with 3 mm allowance
Nozzle and flange leakage and fatigue at the PSV nozzle
severity_reason: No immediate failure, but there is no pressure margin, so every relief event runs at the design limit.

deviation: Relief above the credited 32.70 kg/s when the HIPPS fails to close at the re-rated rate
causes: SDV-101 fails to close (node 1), or the HIPPS is bypassed or its proof test overdue
The 35% credit is 0.65 x 50.31 kg/s (the +18% case) = 32.70 kg/s; it is only 23.3% below the current 42.63 kg/s case, so the credit is tied to the re-rate
Well potential at 163.4 MMscfd pushing the blocked-outlet case to 50.3 kg/s
consequences: 50.3 kg/s is 107.5% of the 46.34 kg/s flare; radiation 82.4 m against 75.0 m now, beyond the sterile area the study did not verify
Flare flameout and liquid carryover, with a larger radiation contour
severity_reason: The debottlenecked rate is only inside the flare limit because of the HIPPS credit; losing it overloads the flare.

deviation: Simultaneous relief from HP plus MP, LP or fire exceeds 46.34 kg/s
causes: Shared flare header, with the HP blocked outlet coincident with a K-102 or K-103 trip or an MP or LP PSV lift
A fire in another area adding its relief load
No load-shedding or sequential blowdown philosophy in the basis
consequences: Flare above 100% with the HP case alone already at 91.1%; header back pressure rises and PSVs stall
The radiation contour expands beyond 82.4 m, with possible flameout
severity_reason: A single relief case fills 91% of the flare; any coincidence overloads it.

deviation: SIMOPS: flare-header hot work or tie-in during the four-week shutdown with HP live on another front
causes: Four parallel work fronts, with header and tip work while wells and HP separation remain online
Isolation by a single blind or valve; the water-package tie-in at V-101 is also live
Hot-work permit over a hydrocarbon-bearing system
consequences: Ignition of a hydrocarbon release with the flare path removed (node 7 loss of flare)
Injury or fatality potential and loss of the relief path for the live HP train
severity_reason: The shutdown is a SIMOPS campaign on a live platform; the risk register rates it low likelihood but the consequence is major.

deviation: Reverse flow from the 25 bara condensate line into the 1.013 bara stock tank
causes: P-101 trip or check-valve failure on the 6 in export line
Reception pressure above 25 bara, or the line shut in at reception
No non-return protection specified at the battery limit
consequences: Near-atmospheric V-104 overpressured by up to 25 bara, with tank rupture and a 2,936 bbl/d condensate release and fire
Reverse flow also carries water and wax back into the tank
severity_reason: A 25 bara line connected back to an atmospheric tank through a check valve is a tank-rupture scenario.

deviation: Reception or export-line pressure above 90 bara
causes: Downstream reception shut-in or compression raising the line pressure
Line blockage or hydrate, with thermal expansion of a blocked-in 15 km line
Reverse flow into the platform 90 bara system (design 100 barg)
consequences: K-101 driven toward surge or stonewall, with the sales mixer and discharge line above 90 bara
Overpressure of the 12 in X65 line (100 barg design) or reverse flow through the compressor
severity_reason: The 100 barg line has margin, but the compressor and the platform system are at their operating limit.

deviation: Water-saturated export gas: hydrate and corrosion in the 15 km line
causes: No dehydration; the aftercooler at 313.15 K leaves the gas saturated at of order 15 kg/MMscf against a typical 3 kg/MMscf line specification
CO2 at 1.22 mol% in the vapour, and seabed cooldown to below 10 C at 60 bara reception
No hydrate or corrosion inhibitor downstream of the platform
consequences: Hydrate plug at 60 bara and low temperature, with loss of export and pressure build-up at the platform
Wet CO2 corrosion of X65 with 3 mm allowance over 15 km, and slugging or water dropout at reception
severity_reason: A hydrate plug or a corrosion leak in a 15 km, 60-90 bara gas line is a major-accident and supply-loss scenario.

deviation: Partial blockage (hydrate, wax, pig or debris) in the 12 in gas or 6 in condensate line
causes: Hydrate or wax deposition, a stuck pig, or 3LPP and debris in the line
Partial isolation or a restricted reception valve
consequences: Backpressure rises, K-101 approaches surge, and the rate falls below 161.8 MMscfd
Overpressure between the blockage and the platform, and pig or line damage
severity_reason: A partial blockage degrades rate and loads the compressor; escalation needs the line to fully block.

deviation: Pipeline blowdown or pigging to the platform flare exceeds 46.34 kg/s
causes: The 12 in by 15 km line at 60-90 bara holds of order 55 t of gas and its blowdown is routed to the flare
Pigging, depressurisation, or an emergency shutdown venting to the flare
No restriction or staged blowdown in the basis
consequences: Initial blowdown rate far above the 46.34 kg/s flare design, with flare overload and radiation beyond 82.4 m
Liquid carryover to the flare and possible flameout
severity_reason: Routine pipeline depressurisation can exceed the flare design by a large factor, and the flare is the only sink.
